clue.text: Checking very hot stuff about one sort of atom

indicators.note: about here signals that the word for hot stuff is turned round

parts.note: fire is hot stuff
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cation is a positively charged ion, an atom carrying a charge

explanation.surface: A scientist examining dangerously hot material around a particular kind of atom.
explanation.definitionFit: Verifying something means confirming it is true, which is the same as checking it.

clue.text: Disappear without right coat, clearly

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for disappear goes around the letter for right

parts.note: to vanish is to disappear

explanation.surface: Someone vanishes without the right coat on, obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: VANISH wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is a transparent finish, so it is a coat applied that you can see through.

clue.text: Teacher's talk cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word for talk is lopped off

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for to talk at length

explanation.surface: A teacher's lecture gets cut off before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last letter, T, from RABBIT; 'rabbit' is everyday British slang for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and religious teacher.

clue.text: Very good hand from crowded theatre

definitions.meaning: in poker, three of a kind plus a pair is a strong holding
a venue with every seat sold is said to have this

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a strong poker holding and a sold-out auditorium.

clue.text: Irascible Conservative behind the times

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the UK political party
rusty means out of practice, no longer up to date

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered Tory politician who is out of touch with modern life.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusty describes someone gruff and short-tempered, which is irascible.

clue.text: United play, perhaps, showing this?

parts.note: reads like a remark on a football side such as Manchester United, but asks what quality a united, cooperating group displays

explanation.definitionFit: Collaboration between members of a group is the quality shown when people play together as one.

clue.text: Source of light or dark blue awarded here?

definitions.meaning: a bay window projecting from an upper storey lets light in
dark blue is the Oxford colour, and an Oxford college is where such a blue might be won

explanation.walkthrough: Oxford sportsmen win a 'blue' and Oxford's colour is dark blue; Oriel is one of its colleges, and an oriel is a kind of bay window.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a projecting window and an Oxford college, home of dark-blue sporting honours.

clue.text: Vessel's doctor operating inside port

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for operating is placed within the doctor abbreviation

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
a machine that is operating is on
Hull is an English port on the Humber

explanation.surface: A ship's doctor at work within a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the operating word within the doctor's abbreviation; Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, England. The 's stands for 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A monohull is a boat with a single hull, as opposed to a catamaran.

clue.text: Take off when clubs close

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: Golfers leave at the moment the clubhouse shuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise into the air, as an aircraft does when it takes off.

clue.text: Starts off really early, before even larks rise

indicators.note: the starts of the words that follow are taken, one initial from each

explanation.surface: An early riser beats even the larks out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Larks are early-rising birds, which makes 'rise' look like getting up rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against authority, as in a rising or revolt.

clue.text: Without dissent, United Nations backed North America and Finland

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: backed means each of the following words is written backwards

parts.note: Suomi is the Finnish name for Finland

explanation.surface: The UN unanimously supported North America and Finland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns each of the two country abbreviations round in place; Suomi is the name Finns use for their own country.
explanation.definitionFit: When everyone agrees and nobody objects, the decision is unanimous.

clue.text: Cook writes his recipe

indicators.note: to cook figures or books is to falsify them by rearranging, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A chef writes down how to make one of his dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the chef or the definition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a classic dish of mutton, potato and onion, the kind of thing a recipe gives.

clue.text: Free and easy

definitions.meaning: free here means not tied up or confined
easy here means relaxed and slack, as in easy-fitting clothes

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something unrestrained as well as something slack or relaxed.

clue.text: Buzzing noise insect makes to deceive

parts.note: a hum is a buzzing noise
a bug is an insect

explanation.surface: A buzzing sound an insect makes in order to fool something.
explanation.definitionFit: To humbug someone is to trick or delude them.

clue.text: Abuse a drug dispensed for biker's protection

parts.note: mud is abuse, as in slinging mud at someone

indicators.note: a drug that is dispensed is made up, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Misusing a drug that a pharmacist has dispensed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudguard is a curved shield over a motorcycle wheel keeping dirt off the rider.

clue.text: Abysmal professional cast

parts.note: pro is short for professional
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A professional actor company described as terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abysmal' reads as 'awful' but is used in its literal sense of bottomless.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal literally means like an abyss, deep beyond measure.

clue.text: Pick prize plant grown in this

parts.note: the flower of something is its pick, the best part
a pot is a prize, such as a trophy or a pool of winnings

explanation.surface: Choose the award-winning plant raised here.
explanation.definitionFit: A container of earth in which a plant is raised is what this pot is for.

clue.text: Bitterly scornful of cords in a tangle

indicators.note: cords in a tangle are knotted and jumbled, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a mess of knotted cords.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic describes grimly mocking, cynical contempt.

clue.text: Archaic old word for "wash", the same when reversed

indicators.note: when reversed tells us the two words just given are read back to front

parts.note: lave is a literary, old-fashioned verb meaning to wash
idem is Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A remark that an old term for washing reads identically backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a palindrome, but 'the same' is IDEM; 'when reversed' turns LAVE+IDEM into MEDIEVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something medieval belongs to the Middle Ages, so it is very old-fashioned.

clue.text: Change smart teenager once provided over a year

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the earlier pieces sit above the letter for year

parts.note: Mods were sharply dressed 1960s British youth subculture members
if means provided, as in 'provided that'
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A well-dressed adolescent from the past changed, given a year.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were stylish 1960s British youths on scooters.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something is to alter it.

clue.text: Model surgical procedure for lump

parts.note: a doll is a model of a person
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A model having an operation to remove a growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless blob of something soft, such as cream.

clue.text: At first sight, it's absurd as soldier joins up, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the following is judged by its sound, not spelling

parts.note: a para (paratrooper) is a soldier, and docks means joins up, as spacecraft do

explanation.surface: It seems crazy when a soldier enlists, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins up' looks like enlisting but means docks; PARA DOCKS said quickly gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a statement that seems self-contradictory but may hold true.

clue.text: Behaving like a star, when one's out in test

parts.note: as can mean when

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for one leaves the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Acting like a celebrity when one is out batting in a cricket test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes I from TRIAL to leave TRAL. A Test is an international cricket match, adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means relating to or resembling the stars.

clue.text: Alarm daughter, being pursued by another relative

indicators.note: being pursued by means the first piece is followed by the next

parts.note: an aunt is another family relative

explanation.surface: A girl is frightened while being chased by her aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt someone is to intimidate or dismay them.

clue.text: Ham going off after a short time

indicators.note: after places the word for going off behind the abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
meat or game going off is said to be high

explanation.surface: A ham that has gone bad after a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' suggests meat, but it is the back of the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The ham is the back of the thigh, part of the upper leg.

clue.text: Ted primes in order to paint

indicators.note: putting things in order means rearranging them, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Ted prepares a surface so that he can paint it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primes' makes the surface about undercoating, which suits a paint answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a water-based paint for walls.

clue.text: Sound fruit's sound

indicators.note: the second sound signals a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

explanation.surface: Healthy fruit is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Sound' is the verb, to measure depth; the second is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb water is to measure its depth with a weighted line.

clue.text: Stranger demanding free gin or rum

indicators.note: rum here is the adjective meaning odd, so these letters come out strangely

explanation.surface: An outsider asks for free gin or rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like a drink beside gin but means strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner is someone from another country, an outsider.

clue.text: Poet's pen

definitions.meaning: Ezra ... was an American modernist poet
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both Ezra the modernist writer and an enclosure for stray animals.

clue.text: Pretty, sweet, little tree

parts.note: a chocolate is a sweet
box is a small evergreen tree or shrub

explanation.surface: A pretty little sweet-scented tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Chocolate-box describes a pretty, sentimental scene like those printed on sweet boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate-box is used of something conventionally and sentimentally pretty, like a thatched cottage.
